messages:
elaine: Customer ticket #T-12345 — saw a regression in p95/p99 since Sat 09:00 UTC, multiple requests hitting p99 ~6s (baseline ~0.7s). Customer attached traces and a few request IDs. Can infra take a look?
ops-bot: ALERT: prod /v1/generate route p99 spike: 6.12s, p95: 1.85s — grafana: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/latency
ian: thanks — can you paste a minimal repro + one request-id so we can trace through logs?
elaine: repro curl they ran: ```curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer *****' -d '{"model":"rwd-3.2-large","input":"short prompt","max_tokens":256}'``` request-id: req_20260315_8a7b
devin: looking at provisioner logs for the dedicated pool used by this customer (pool: eu-dedicated-gpu-x). I see attach queue growing at 08:58 UTC, provisioner hitting 429 from cloud API: "RateLimitExceeded: attach calls per-minute exceeded" then exponential backoff => attach attempts delayed. snippet: ```2026-03-15T08:58:12Z provisioner INFO attach req=req_20260315_8a7b status=queued queue_len=43``` ```2026-03-15T08:58:14Z cloudapi WARN 429 attach call rate-limited backoff=2s``` ```2026-03-15T08:59:01Z provisioner INFO backoff increased backoff=8s```
tim: cloud region had reduced spare capacity earlier (spot reclaim / maintenance), so instance allocation attempts started failing — autoscaler then hit our internal attach-rate limit to avoid hammering cloud API. net result: requests waited in attach queue until warm GPUs became available.
maria: confirm pool saturation: eu-dedicated-gpu-x nodes=24/25 used, min=1, max=25, spike of concurrent attach requests from several big customers. autoscaler strategy kept min low to save cost, so cold starts piled up.
ian: can we do a short-term mitigation? increase min for that pool and temporarily route that customer to hosted fallback model?
aj: immediate actions I can run now: 1) bump pool min to 6, 2) enable prewarm=true on pool, 3) add a routing rule to send this customer's traffic to hosted fallback route with smaller model if attach queue > 10. commands: ```redwoodctl pool update eu-dedicated-gpu-x --min 6 --prewarm true && redwoodctl routes add-fallback --customer T-12345 --when attach_queue_gt=10 --fallback hosted:rwd-3.2-small``` I'll execute after 👍
elaine: please run — customer is getting fairly upset, SLA note in ticket.
aj: running step 1.. (exec) ```> redwoodctl pool update eu-dedicated-gpu-x --min 6 --prewarm true
OK: pool eu-dedicated-gpu-x updated (min=6 prewarm=on)```
support-bot: automated: pool eu-dedicated-gpu-x scaled to 6 prewarmed nodes — expected warmup 90s
ian: any telemetry after the change?
devin: within ~3m of the prewarm completed, p99 dropped to ~1.1s, p95 ~0.6s. grafana: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/latency?from=1768501200&to=1768502100
ops-bot: ALERT RESOLVED: p99 back to baseline ~1.1s
maria: good short-term. follow-ups: 1) change autoscaler backoff: don't exponentially increase attach backoff above 2s for dedicated pools with quota near capacity, 2) add preemptive warmup policy for customers with heavy sustained QPS, 3) add alert when attach_queue > 10 for >2m.
ian: agree. Dev backlog item and postmortem required. aj can you open a Jira with proposed code/ops changes?
aj: created RW-9876: "autoscaler: cap attach backoff & prewarm policy" link: https://jira.redwood/browse/RW-9876
elaine: I'll update customer T-12345 with mitigation steps and ETA for permanent fixes. thanks team. :white_check_mark:
